what_happened.line: The TCP Building Design Committee reached informal consensus to ask for added design funding, a wider charge (building and/or land), and two products: preserve or build new.
The committee will remove language about the future use of other vacated buildings from its Select Board letter; the chair will simplify it to bullets for review.
A member will draft three warrant articles: an update report, a charge change, and funding.
Members said the architects' design budget is spent while final documents and a town meeting presentation are still owed.
No formal votes on the asks were taken; the January 13 minutes were approved and meetings were set for March 9, March 17, April 7 and April 21.

why_it_matters: Further design money for the town center building project would need an appropriation, so residents may be asked to vote on funding and a changed committee charge at Town Meeting.

The financial advisor's debt scenarios for this project and Turkey Hill were described as fitting the town's debt ratios, with 20-year versions still to come, so the borrowing cost is not yet settled.
watch_next: March 9 Select Board appearance, where the committee will present its requests; later meetings set for March 17, April 7 and April 21.
The three draft warrant articles, and an architect's estimate for further design that the town manager said should be pinned down soon for the finance committee.

Members noted the estimate showed little identified savings from removing phasing.
Demolition of TC Passios and the old primary were discussed as similar, with abatement included.
A member said the cost is higher than the number people had in mind and cited program scope and escalation.
Members cited lumber and pandemic-driven price increases affecting estimates.
A breakdown of site work and parking costs was requested.
A member said the town manager sees no budgetary problem absorbing the project if work starts next year and debt comes on in the later years.
A resident asked how much has been spent; the article amount was recalled approximately.

decisions.decision: Consensus without a motion to send specific questions to the design team: best-and-final pricing, savings from single phase, HVAC/electrical and site work breakdowns, and reasoning for reduced contingency.
Chair to work with the town manager on how to procure extra architect services for a sharpened tear-down and rebuild estimate.
Target a Select Board presentation, asking for agenda time on March 9, after the committee's March 3 meeting; keep March 3 and March 17 meetings posted.
Chair to draft a communication to the Select Board for the next meeting.
Chair to follow up with the new DPW head on paving through the pavement management plan, cheaper curbing and maintenance.

what_happened.line: The committee reached consensus, without a motion, to send the design team questions seeking best-and-final pricing and a breakdown of HVAC, electrical and site work.
The questions also ask what single-phase construction would save and why the design contingency was reduced; members found the renovation estimate too high.
The chair is to work with the town manager on procuring extra architect services for a sharper tear-down and rebuild estimate; the current comparison is a rough ballpark only.
The committee aims to present to the Select Board, asking for agenda time on March 9, and keeps its March 3 and March 17 meetings posted.
No vote was taken on cost or on a recommendation; the meeting adjourned by roll call.

why_it_matters: The cost of renovating TC Passios, and whether to tear down and rebuild instead, is still unsettled, so what the project would add to the town budget and to taxes through debt is not yet known.

Any figure that goes to Town Meeting will rest on the architect's answers on contingency, phasing and site work, and residents at that vote will be asked to judge a project whose price is still being tested.
watch_next: March 3 committee meeting, then the Select Board presentation the committee hopes to schedule for March 9.
The design team's answers on best-and-final pricing, and any extra architect estimate for tear-down and rebuild.
